headline: Chip crash drags S&P 500 into correction
context: Chipmakers led a broad AI sell-off, and a report that the SEC is looking into Nvidia's accounting added to the gloom.

GPN.text: Jumped on reports that private equity firm GTCR is weighing a takeover of the payments company worth about $50 billion.

GIS.text: No company news. Packaged food makers rose together, and consumer staples was the only sector to gain.

MKC.text: No company news. It rose alongside food peers such as General Mills as staples stocks held up.

SNDK.text: Market tracker TrendForce warned that flash memory prices are falling and Chinese cloud firms may cut orders next year.

BE.text: Sold off with other AI infrastructure stocks, as power equipment peers such as Vertiv also fell sharply.

NVDA.text: Chipmakers sank together, and Reuters reported that the SEC is looking into Nvidia's accounting.

watch.title: Inflation and GDP data
watch.text: PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, plus a revised growth figure for Q3.

watch.title: Thanksgiving closure
watch.text: US stock markets shut for the holiday, then open for a half day on Friday.

question: Is the AI sell-off a healthy reset or a sign of deeper trouble?
